name: Manganese tripeptide-1

lead: Manganese tripeptide-1 is a cosmetic peptide complex used in facial serums for photodamaged skin. It is described as a manganese counterpart of the copper peptide GHK.
A single 12-week facial study reported improvement in photodamage signs, especially pigmentation, as judged by participants and a blinded investigator.

paras: The published study does not establish a mechanism; the ingredient is presented as an analogue of GHK-type peptides.
The one study reported good tolerability with no significant inflammation. Long-term and comparative safety data have not been published in the sources reviewed.

studies.title: Topical manganese peptide in the treatment of photodamaged skin.
studies.source: Journal of cosmetic and laser therapy : official publication of the European Society for Laser Dermatology

lead: Manganese tripeptide-1 is a cosmetic ingredient consisting of a manganese complex of a tripeptide, described as the manganese analogue of the copper-binding peptide GHK. It is used in facial serums marketed for photodamaged skin, including uneven pigmentation.

The published human evidence is limited to a single open-label-style facial study in which participants used a serum containing the complex twice daily for up to 12 weeks. The investigators reported improvement in several photodamage signs, most notably hyperpigmentation, and good tolerability [1]. Independent controlled trials have not been identified.

paras: The ingredient appears in topical serums aimed at signs of facial photoaging such as discoloration and rough texture [1].

One published study evaluated a facial serum containing manganese tripeptide-1 applied twice a day for up to 12 weeks. Participants and a blinded investigator noted improvement in several photodamage parameters, predominantly those linked to hyperpigmentation, with overall photodamage ranking moving from moderate to mild on average. The authors reported no significant skin inflammation attributable to the complex [1]. The report describes a serum formulation rather than the isolated ingredient, and no comparison against other treatments is described in the abstract.

The copper form, GHK-Cu, was first isolated from human plasma by Loren Pickart in 1973 and is marketed as copper tripeptide-1 [2]. Evidence for GHK-Cu in facial anti-aging is described in Wikipedia as coming mostly from cell and animal work plus small, short facial studies [2].
